visual.general_description: Four-panel composite (A-D) of radiographic barium contrast studies of the neck, chest and upper abdomen, each panel marked with a red letter at bottom-left.
visual.detailed_description: A single 776 x 239 px row of four grayscale/cyan-tinted radiographs lettered A, B, C, D in red. All show bright positive contrast in an upper-gastrointestinal conduit with variable dilatation, narrowing and tortuosity; panel A shows a large lobulated dilated segment in a small patient, panel B a neck pouch with narrow tract and large dilated sac, panel C an irregular tortuous column with parallel tube-like lines, and panel D a very thin tortuous channel with a pharyngeal contrast pool. Some panels carry partial overlay text ("1/2", "EST", "EQUEST") that is not interpretable. The caption only states "(A,B,C,D) barium image studies" and does not map panels to patients, views or findings.

panels.general_description: Barium contrast study of a small patient: dense contrast fills a markedly dilated, lobulated segment in the lower chest/upper abdomen with a narrow contrast channel rising toward the neck.
panels.detailed_description: Panel A (letter A in red at bottom-left) is a frontal/slightly oblique radiograph of the head-neck-chest-upper abdomen of a small patient with a relatively large head. Bright positive contrast outlines a large, irregular, fold-like (haustra-like) dilated segment occupying the lower chest and upper abdomen on the image left; a thin contrast column runs upward from it toward the neck/lower face region. Ribs, spine and soft-tissue outlines are faintly seen. Overlay text "1" and "1/2" is readable at the top-left; further text is cropped or unreadable. No arrows, scale bar or measurement are visible.

panels.general_description: Barium contrast study, frontal chest/neck view: contrast in a neck pouch, a narrow descending tract and a large dilated contrast-filled sac in the right chest, with a diagonal tube-like line at the upper chest.
panels.detailed_description: Panel B (letter B in red at bottom-left) is a frontal chest radiograph. A bright contrast-filled pouch lies in the neck/upper mediastinum; a narrow, slightly tortuous contrast tract descends from it to a large, smooth, dilated contrast-filled sac in the lower right hemithorax (image left) with a smaller adjacent lobule below. A separate thin contrast streak runs along the left (image right) lower thorax beside the spine. A thin diagonal radiopaque linear structure crosses the upper chest. Lungs, ribs and spine are visible; the partial overlay text "EST" appears at upper left. No arrows, measurements or scale are visible.

panels.general_description: Barium contrast study, lateral/oblique neck-chest view: irregular tortuous contrast column from the neck to a rounded contrast bulb, with parallel tube-like radiopaque lines.
panels.detailed_description: Panel C (letter C in red at bottom-left) is a lateral/oblique radiograph of neck and chest. An irregular, tortuous, variably wide contrast column descends from the neck/upper thorax to a rounded contrast-filled bulb at the lower left of the field; a large soft contrast-filled structure is cut off at the bottom right edge. Parallel thin, tubular radiopaque lines with double contours run through the thorax alongside the contrast column. Spine, ribs and lung fields are visible. Partial overlay text "EQUEST" appears at upper left. No arrows, measurements or scale are visible.

panels.general_description: Barium contrast study, lateral head-neck-upper chest view: contrast in pharynx and a very narrow, tortuous contrast channel descending to a rounded contrast bulb.
panels.detailed_description: Panel D (letter D in red at bottom-left) is a lateral radiograph of head, neck and upper chest. A bright contrast pool lies in the pharynx/oral region at the top. A very thin, tortuous, partly looped or beaded contrast channel descends anterior to the cervical and thoracic spine and ends in a rounded contrast-filled bulb at the bottom of the field. A thin curved radiopaque line arches across the neck. The vertebral column is clearly visible with small ring-like lucent markings. Partial letters at the left margin are unreadable. No arrows, measurements or scale are visible.
